overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficiently detailed June 3, 2013 executive session minutes, but its July 30, 2014 revisions cured the defect, so no further relief was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 3, 2013 executive session minutes were not sufficiently detailed for a member of the public to understand the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficiently detailed executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 3, 2013 executive session minutes failed to list all documents used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The executive session minutes were also revised on that date to include a listing of the documents referenced during the executive session.

allegations.summary: The minutes used the acronym "WTA" for the Wayland Teachers Association; the AG addressed whether this alone violated the law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not, however, find that the use of "WTA" violated the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
